sentences.ko: 주말에 진짜 아무것도 안 했는데, 이상하게 그게 딱 필요했던 것 같아. 하루 종일 소파에 누워서 폰만 보다가 하루가 다 갔거든.
sentences.text: I literally did nothing all weekend, but honestly that's exactly what I needed, because I just lay on the couch scrolling on my phone until the day was gone.

alts.text: I did nothing this weekend, like actually nothing, and I'm not even mad because I just stayed on the couch on my phone all day.
I did absolutely nothing all weekend, but it was precisely what I needed, as I spent the entire day on the sofa looking at my phone.

sentences.note: **literally** 는 '진짜, 완전히' 정도로 가볍게 씁니다. 폰 들여다보는 건 **scrolling on my phone** 이 제일 흔하고, 캐주얼한 **I'm not even mad** 는 '그래도 후회는 없다'는 느낌이에요.
sentences.situation: 주말에 아무것도 안 하고 쉰 게 좋았다고 말하기

sentences.ko: 시킨 거랑 완전히 다른 게 왔는데, 다시 시키자니 한 시간은 더 걸릴 것 같고 그냥 이거 먹어야 하나 싶어.
sentences.text: They sent me something completely different from what I ordered, and if I reorder it's going to take another hour, so I'm kind of tempted to just eat this.

alts.text: They got my order completely wrong, and I'm not waiting another hour for a redo, so I'll probably just eat what showed up.
What arrived is not what I ordered, and placing another order would mean waiting an additional hour, so I am inclined to simply keep this one.

sentences.note: **kind of tempted to** ~ 는 '그냥 ~할까 싶다' 하는 미묘한 느낌입니다. **showed up** 은 '(생각과 다른 게) 오다'라는 뜻이고, 격식 있게 말할 땐 **I am inclined to** ~ 를 씁니다.
sentences.situation: 배달 시켰는데 엉뚱한 게 와서 얘기하기

sentences.ko: 도와주고는 싶은데 이번 주는 진짜 정신이 없어서, 괜히 맡았다가 제대로 못 해 주면 오히려 너한테 더 민폐일 것 같아.
sentences.text: I'd really like to help, but this week is honestly insane for me, and if I take it on and do a bad job, that just makes things worse for you.

alts.text: I'd love to help but I'm slammed this week, and honestly you'd be worse off with me doing it badly than with me just saying no.
I would be glad to help, but my schedule this week is extremely tight, and taking it on without doing it properly would not serve you well.

sentences.note: **take it on** 은 '떠맡다'입니다. 바쁘다는 말로는 **slammed** 를 자주 쓰고(swamped 도 같은 뜻), 격식 있게는 **my schedule this week is extremely tight** 처럼 말합니다.

sentences.ko: 이번엔 진짜 될 줄 알았는데 또 삼일 만에 무너졌어. 저녁까지는 잘 참다가 밤에 배고파지면 도저히 안 되더라고.
sentences.text: I really thought I'd stick with it this time, but I caved after three days, because I can hold out until dinner and then the late night hunger just wins.

alts.text: I was so sure I'd last this time but I caved on day three, since I'm fine till dinner and then late night me takes over.
I genuinely expected to keep it up this time, but I gave in after three days, as I manage well until dinner and struggle later in the evening.

sentences.note: **cave** 와 **give in** 둘 다 '참다가 무너지다'입니다. **stick with it** 은 계속 유지하다, **hold out** 은 버티다예요.

sentences.ko: 이사를 갈까 싶다가도, 지금 집이 딱히 나쁜 것도 아닌데 괜히 돈이랑 시간만 버리는 거 아닌가 싶어서 계속 미루고 있어.
sentences.text: Part of me wants to move, but the place I'm in now isn't actually bad, so I keep wondering if I'd just be wasting money and time, and I put it off.

alts.text: I keep thinking about moving but my place is honestly fine, so I go back and forth and end up putting it off every single time.
I have been considering a move, but my current place is perfectly adequate, so I am not convinced it would be worth the cost and the effort.

sentences.note: **Part of me wants to** ~ 는 '~하고 싶은 마음도 있다'. **go back and forth** 는 결정 못 하고 오락가락한다는 뜻이고, **put it off** 는 미루다입니다.
